pages.text: This is Barcelona. It is a sunny city in Spain.
pages.about: Barcelona is the second biggest city in Spain, after Madrid. It sits by the Mediterranean Sea, so it is warm and sunny a lot of the year. It is the main city of Catalonia, a part of Spain with its own language and traditions.

pages.text: People here say hola. They speak Catalan and Spanish.
pages.about: In Barcelona people speak two languages: Catalan and Spanish. 'Hola' (OH-la) means hello in both! 'Bon dia' means good morning in Catalan, and 'gràcies' means thank you. In Spanish, thank you is 'gracias'.

pages.text: The flag of Spain is red and yellow.
pages.about: The flag of Spain has a red stripe, a wide yellow stripe, and another red stripe, with a coat of arms on one side. Barcelona also flies the flag of Catalonia, called the senyera, which has four red stripes on yellow.

pages.text: Barcelona has a beach. You can build sandcastles!
pages.about: Barcelona is a big city with beaches right next to it. The most famous is Barceloneta beach. People swim, play volleyball, build sandcastles, and eat ice cream by the sea. The sea there is the Mediterranean Sea.

pages.text: This big church is still being built!
pages.about: The Sagrada Família is a giant church. Builders started it in 1882, more than 140 years ago, and they are still working on it today! A famous architect named Antoni Gaudí designed it. He said, 'My client is not in a hurry.' When it is done it will have 18 tall towers, and the middle one will be the tallest church tower in the world.

pages.text: Inside, the columns look like tall trees.
pages.about: Gaudí loved nature. Inside the Sagrada Família the stone columns split into branches at the top, like a forest of trees. Colorful windows make rainbow light on the walls, blue and green on one side and orange and red on the other. It feels like being in a magic forest.

pages.text: This house has a roof like a dragon's back.
pages.about: Casa Batlló is a house that Gaudí redesigned. The roof is curvy and covered in shiny tiles, like the scales on a dragon's back. Some people say the tower with a cross is the sword of Saint George, who fought the dragon in an old story. The balconies look like masks, and there are almost no straight lines anywhere!

pages.text: In this park, a colorful dragon guards the stairs.
pages.about: Park Güell is a park on a hill, made by Gaudí. At the entrance stairs there is a big colorful lizard or dragon that people call 'El Drac'. It is covered in a mosaic made from little broken pieces of tiles, called trencadís. Kids love to take photos with it. The park also has gingerbread-looking houses and a long wavy bench covered in tiles.

pages.text: Dip a churro in hot chocolate. Yum!
pages.about: Churros are long sticks of fried dough, crispy outside and soft inside, often sprinkled with sugar. In Spain people dip them into very thick hot chocolate, so thick that a churro can almost stand up in it! People also love tapas, which are lots of small plates of food to share.

pages.text: People stand on shoulders to make tall human towers.
pages.about: In Catalonia, teams build human towers called castells (cas-TAYS). Strong people stand at the bottom, and others climb up and stand on their shoulders, level after level, sometimes 9 or 10 levels high! The smallest and lightest child climbs to the very top, wearing a helmet, and raises a hand to wave. Their motto is 'strength, balance, courage and good sense'.

pages.text: Lots of people here love football.
pages.about: Barcelona has a famous football (soccer) team, FC Barcelona, called Barça. Their shirts are blue and dark red. Their stadium, Camp Nou, is the biggest football stadium in Europe. When the team scores, the whole stadium cheers so loudly you can hear it streets away!

pages.text: At night, a magic fountain dances to music.
pages.about: The Magic Fountain of Montjuïc was built in 1929. On some evenings it puts on a show: the water jumps and dances to music, and colored lights turn it pink, blue, green and gold. Lots of families sit on the steps to watch.

pages.text: Adéu, Barcelona! Which city did you like best?
pages.about: Adéu (ah-DAY-oo) means goodbye in Catalan. In Spanish it is 'adiós'. You have now visited Paris, London and Barcelona. More cities are coming soon!
